---
title: "Runway milestones"
description: "How OPDI finds the line-up, the moment a runway is vacated, aircraft taxiing across a runway, and go-arounds. None of them has been validated."
---

## What it is

Besides the take-off and the landing (see
[Take-off and landing](takeoff-landing.qmd)), OPDI publishes five more events
about the use of runways:

| Event type | Moment | Standard number |
|---|---|---|
| `line-up` | A departing aircraft enters the runway to take off. | T06 |
| `runway-vacated` | An arriving aircraft leaves the runway after landing. | T19 |
| `runway-crossing-entry` | A taxiing aircraft enters a runway in order to cross it. | none |
| `runway-crossing-vacated` | The same aircraft leaves the runway on the other side. | none |
| `go-around` | An aircraft on its approach gives up the landing and climbs away. The event is placed at the lowest point of the approach. | none |

The standard numbers are those of airport collaborative decision making
(A-CDM; see [Take-off and landing](takeoff-landing.qmd#what-it-is)). A runway
crossing and a go-around have no number there.

The time between `ALDT` (touchdown) and `runway-vacated` is the **runway
occupancy time** of an arrival. The time between `line-up` and `ATOT` (take-off)
is the time a departure spends on the runway.

The first four events carry, in `info`, the airport (`apt_icao`), the runway
direction (`runway`), the true bearing of its centre line
(`runway_bearing_deg`), the class of the runway pass (`traversal_class`), the
angle between the runway and the aircraft's direction of travel over the
ground (its ground track) (`align_deg`, degrees), the
highest ground speed in the pass (`max_gs_kt`, knots) and the standard number
(`milestone`). A `go-around` carries the destination airport, the lowest height
above the airport (`low_height_ft`), the highest rate of climb afterwards
(`recovery_roc_ft_min`, feet per minute) and the duration of the excursion
(`excursion_seconds`). All five carry a position, an altitude, the distance
flown and the time passed. The events carry the version `events_v0.3.0`.

## How it is computed

### Line-up, runway vacated and runway crossings

These events come from the same **runway passes** as the take-off and landing
times: runs of state vectors on or just short of one runway, classified as a
departure, an arrival or a crossing. The construction of a pass, the runway
grid and the choice of the runway direction are described on
[Take-off and landing](takeoff-landing.qmd#how-it-is-computed).

1. **`line-up`** is the first state vector of a departure pass that lies on the
   runway itself, between the two thresholds.
2. **`runway-vacated`** is the last state vector of an arrival pass that lies
   on the runway.
3. A pass is a **crossing** when all of these hold:
   - the aircraft's median ground track is at least 45° away from the runway's
     bearing;
   - its ground speed never exceeds 40 kt;
   - the pass lasts at most 120 s;
   - the aircraft is less than 15 ft above the airport at the start and at the
     end of the pass.
4. **`runway-crossing-entry`** is the first state vector of a crossing pass and
   **`runway-crossing-vacated`** the last.

All four are taken at a received state vector, not interpolated. A crossing is
published under its own names so that it can never be counted as a take-off
or a landing.

### Go-around

A go-around may be abandoned before the aircraft reaches the runway, so this
detector does not use runway passes. It works on the height of the aircraft
above its destination airport (barometric altitude minus the airport's
elevation).

1. Find each time the height falls through 500 ft, and each time it rises
   through 1,500 ft. A dead band of 50 ft on each side prevents an aircraft
   flying level near one of these heights from producing a series of
   crossings. The moments are interpolated between samples.
2. Pair each rise through 1,500 ft with the last fall through 500 ft before
   it. This interval is one **excursion**. Only the first rise after a fall is
   used.
3. Keep the excursion as a go-around when all of these hold:
   - its lowest point is more than 15 ft above the airport, so the aircraft
     did not touch down;
   - the aircraft climbed at 500 ft/min or more at some point in the
     excursion, so it climbed away rather than just stopped descending;
   - the lowest point is at most 10 NM from the destination airport.
4. The event is placed at the lowest point of the excursion.

The 15 ft limit is the same as the one that defines the touchdown time, so a
go-around and a touchdown can never describe the same descent.

## Reference data

None. The airport operator records used for the take-off, landing and block
times (see [Take-off and landing](takeoff-landing.qmd#reference-data)) give no
time for the line-up, for leaving the runway or for crossing it. They hold one
record per movement, so a go-around leaves no record of its own. No other
source of these events was available.

## Validation method

Not validated. Validation would need:

- for `line-up` and `runway-vacated`: times recorded by the airport, for
  example from a surface movement radar or from the A-CDM system of the
  airport;
- for runway crossings: a record of runway crossings from air traffic
  control or a surface movement radar;
- for `go-around`: a list of go-arounds from air traffic control or from the
  airport. A first, weaker check would compare the share of approaches that
  end in a go-around with the rates published in the literature.

The runway that these events name is the same as for the take-off and landing
times of the same pass. That runway was checked for take-offs and landings
(see [Take-off and landing](takeoff-landing.qmd#results)).

## Limitations

- None of these events has been compared with reference data. Their timing
  and their counts are unchecked.
- They need the aircraft to be received on the runway. Many airports have no
  receiver close enough, and there the events are missing.
- They need runways in OurAirports, at an airport that the flight list names
  for the flight.
- A runway pass needs at least one state vector with an altitude. ADS-B
  position messages sent on the ground carry no altitude, so a pass seen only
  through them is not classified, and gives no event. This hits runway
  crossings hardest, because the aircraft is on the ground throughout.
- `line-up`, `runway-vacated` and the crossings are received state vectors,
  so they can be up to one sampling interval (5 s) away from the real moment.
  Runway occupancy times computed from them carry that error at both ends.
- If reception stops while the aircraft is still on the runway, the pass ends
  there, and `runway-vacated` is placed at the last state vector received,
  which is too early. Nothing in the data marks this case.
- For a crossing, the runway is right but its direction (for example `07`
  rather than `25`) is arbitrary: an aircraft crossing at right angles does
  not point along either. Do not count crossings per runway direction.
- A pass whose ground track is between 30° and 45° from the runway is neither a
  departure, an arrival nor a crossing, and gives no event.
- A go-around whose approach never goes below 500 ft above the airport, or
  whose climb-away never reaches 1,500 ft, is not found. A flight without a
  destination airport gets no go-around.
- When two state vectors share the lowest height of an excursion, the one used
  for the go-around time can change from one run to the next.
